note: THE single definition of how everything in this monorepo looks. design.css is GENERATED from this file by build_css.py -- edit this, not the CSS. dev_check.py fails if the two have drifted.

why_not_a_component_library.the_obvious_answer: shadcn/ui on Tailwind + Radix. It is the default reach for a new React app and it is a good one.
why_not_a_component_library.why_it_is_not_used_here: Almost every project in this monorepo is deliberately zero-build: a single HTML file plus vanilla ES modules, served by a stdlib Python server, no npm, no CDN, no bundler. geometry/ says 'no deps, no CDN, no build' as a design goal; earth-heart-beat must work offline as a PWA. Adding React + Tailwind + a bundler to those to get a button component is a bad trade, and a CDN <script> tag is against the offline rule.
why_not_a_component_library.what_is_done_instead: A tokens file plus a hand-written stylesheet and a handful of standards-based custom elements. No framework, no runtime dependency, ~30 KB total.
why_not_a_component_library.the_bridge: Token NAMES follow the shadcn/ui convention (--background, --foreground, --card, --muted, --border, --ring, --radius) so the one React project here (biome-soundscape-designer, Vite + React 18) can adopt real shadcn/ui and map its variables straight onto these values. Same look, two implementations, one source of truth.
why_not_a_component_library.when_to_revisit: If a second build-based app appears, or if the vanilla components start needing focus management and portals beyond what is here, take Radix seriously for those projects and keep this file as the token layer underneath.

palette_provenance.method: The `dataviz` skill's six-check validator (scripts/validate_palette.js), which is what Claude uses for chart palettes. Hues are taken from that skill's validated reference palette rather than invented.

results.core_three_all_pairs: PASS. measured/predicted/refuted (#199e70, #3987e5, #e66767) clear every check on the ALL-PAIRS list, worst normal-vision dE 20.9. These three are the ones that must never be confused and they are safe in any arrangement.
results.full_five_adjacent: PASS on the adjacent pairlist, dark and light. Worst adjacent CVD dE 19.5 (protan) dark, 22.7 light.
results.full_five_all_pairs: FAILS, and that is a documented property of the method rather than a fixable bug -- past three slots no ordering clears the all-pairs floors. The mitigation is the one the method prescribes: every tier badge carries a REQUIRED word or letter and a distinct glyph, so hue never carries meaning alone.
results.what_was_rejected: The palette previously used across these apps (measured #4fb286, predicted #6f8fd0, spec #a06fd0, refuted #c05a5a, explore #d08a4f) FAILS badly: spec and predicted sit dE 2.2 apart under deuteranopia and 10.2 in normal vision. Those two carry OPPOSITE epistemic meaning -- a model prediction against pure speculation -- so that was a real defect, found by running the validator instead of eyeballing it.
results.light_tier_restep: The light-mode TIER colours were re-stepped darker (measured #1baf7a -> #15875e, exploring #eda100 -> #9f6c00, refuted #e34948 -> #df3231, predicted #2a78d6 -> #2976d3) because a badge is text and the originals sat at 2.8, 2.2 and 4.0 against white. Re-validated after: ALL CHECKS PASS on the adjacent pairlist, and the core three still pass ALL-PAIRS (worst CVD dE 9.9 deutan, normal-vision 20.4).

polarize.note: The monorepo's DEFAULT theme as of 2026-08-04 -- a warm-dark adaptation of the Broadsheet design system, handed off as 'Polarize Audio Research System'. Ground/ink scale mapped onto the shadcn-bridge key names below so the same component CSS (.ui-card, .ui-btn, etc.) reskins automatically. Existing consumers keep their current look by opting into [data-theme="dark"] explicitly -- see CLAUDE.md 'Adopted by'. faint-foreground is #6e6050, not the handoff's literal #6b5d4d -- dev_check.py's contrast check caught it at 2.89:1 against the surface colour (below the 3:1 AA-large floor); nudged 3 RGB steps lighter (same hue/warmth ratio) to 3.03:1, computed not eyeballed, same discipline as palette_provenance below.

instrument.note: Added 2026-08-19 from the attend-to-send briefing page, at the operator's request that other projects adopt it. A cool instrument-bench palette rather than the warm Polarize one: near-neutral grounds with a slight blue bias, one phosphor-teal accent, and the semantic pair (measured / open) that carries this repo's central distinction -- what has been measured versus what has not. The accent is the ONLY saturated colour; semantic green/amber are separate from it by design, so 'this is the accent' and 'this is verified' never collide.

instrument-dark.note: The dark half of `instrument`. Applied automatically under prefers-color-scheme when a project selects data-theme="instrument"; see build_css.py.

epistemic.note: The monorepo's real semantic axis, and a RESERVED palette: these colours never double as chart series. Every badge ships colour + word + glyph, so hue is never load-bearing. `weight` orders them; `glyph` is the secondary encoding. LIGHT-MODE STEPS ARE DARKER THAN THE SERIES HUES ON PURPOSE: a tier badge is TEXT, so it is held to 4.5:1 on white, not the 3:1 a chart mark gets. The dark steps already cleared it.

tiers.label: MEASURED
tiers.meaning: Read off the actual render or a real instrument. Never styled like a prediction.

tiers.label: PHYSICS
tiers.meaning: Follows from physics, with the modelling choices named.

tiers.label: [B]
tiers.meaning: Supported by primary literature, with caveats.

tiers.label: PREDICTED
tiers.meaning: Output of a model. Never styled like a measurement.

tiers.label: MODELLED
tiers.meaning: A chosen value that behaves plausibly; not measured.

tiers.label: EXPLORATORY
tiers.meaning: An open question being actively tried. Carries a how-to-kill-it.

tiers.label: [SPEC]
tiers.meaning: Speculative. Tradition, worldbuilding, or a stated guess. Never evidence.

tiers.label: ADDED
tiers.meaning: Something the tool adds that the real thing does not do.

tiers.label: TASTE
tiers.meaning: Invented because it sounds or looks right. Not derived from anything.

tiers.label: REFUTED
tiers.meaning: A claim this project explicitly does NOT make. Carries a scope and a cheapest probe.

series.note: Chart series only. Assigned in fixed order, never cycled, never reused for an epistemic role. Taken unchanged from the dataviz skill's validated reference palette -- do not re-step these by hand.
series.all_pairs_note: Scatter/bubble/small-multiple forms compare every pair at once; only the first three slots clear the all-pairs floors. Past three, fold to Other or facet.
series.relief_rule: Three light-mode slots (aqua, yellow, magenta) sit below 3:1 on the light surface. That is a documented property of the reference palette, not a defect to re-step: the mitigation is the RELIEF RULE -- ship visible direct labels or a table view whenever those slots carry meaning on a light background. dev_check.py asserts the rule is declared rather than asserting a contrast the palette was never designed to meet.

audioInk.note: Spot colours for audio-specific UI under the polarize theme ONLY -- signal/action, human annotation, machine state. NOT interchangeable with `epistemic.families` above: that palette is validated (dataviz 6-check) for a different semantic axis (evidence quality) and must stay reachable even when audioInk is absent (e.g. a non-audio project on the polarize theme). Never reuse a tier colour for audio ink or vice versa. Not yet run through the dataviz validator -- see CLAUDE.md.

clay.use: signal, action, active waveform -- one dominant clay element per view

ochre.use: human annotation only -- markers, note timestamps, citation anchors, bookmarks. Never machine output.

lichen.use: machine state only -- verified, transcribed, synced. Never decorative.

audio.note: Reusable sizing/rendering conventions for audio components -- waveform, spectrogram, transport, region markers. From the Polarize handoff's own 'Rendering guidance': waveforms as SVG paths built from a precomputed peaks array, never full-audio-decode; spectrograms as canvas tiles. See CLAUDE.md for the .ui-waveform/.ui-transport/.ui-spectrogram/.ui-region-marker component classes this backs.

waveform.render: SVG path from a precomputed peaks array -- 'M{x} {top}V{bottom}' per bin
waveform.playedPortion: same path re-stroked in clay, clipped by a rect whose width tracks position

spectrogram.render: canvas, 240 x 60 cells at reference size, six-stop ramp

icons.provenance: MIT licensed, github.com/phosphor-icons/core. Self-hosted as an inline SVG sprite (design/icons/polarize-icons.svg, 15 icons, <symbol> per icon) rather than the full icon-font -- same no-CDN reasoning as the serif font, and lighter (8 KB for the icons actually used vs. the full duotone set).
icons.usage: <svg class="ui-icon"><use href="#ph-play"/></svg> -- a LOCAL fragment, not the file path. design.js fetches and INLINES icons/polarize-icons.svg into the document once (cross-document SVG <use> was tried and found unreliable in-browser -- silent failure, no error), so every consumer references it as a same-document id.

type.sans: Inter, "Inter var", ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, "SF Pro Text", "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
type.mono: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace
type.note: THE INSTRUMENT TRIAD, set 2026-08-19 at the operator's request after the attend-to-send briefing page: DISPLAY is Instrument Serif (headings only), BODY is Inter, LABELS are uppercase IBM Plex Mono with letter-spacing. All three are now SELF-HOSTED under fonts/ (OFL, licence text beside each) -- 76 KB for the three latin subsets together, which is the whole reason this could finally be done: the previous note declined to vendor Inter because it assumed a ~100 KB+ file, and the variable latin subset is 48 KB. Nothing here references a CDN, so the offline-PWA rule (earth-heart-beat and friends) still holds. --font-serif still resolves to Literata for a project that wants a serif for RUNNING TEXT; --font-display is a headline face and must not be used for body copy -- Instrument Serif has no optical-size axis and gets spindly below about 20px.
type.scale_note: Body and subtitle came DOWN on 2026-08-19 (base 15->14, lg 17->15.5) at the operator's request; headings deliberately unchanged. Display sizes are separate and fluid -- see --display-1/2/3 below, which use clamp() so a heading is large on a wide screen without overflowing a phone.

motion.note: Every transition in design.css is wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion.

space_note: Extended to 8/9 (64/96px) on 2026-08-19: app.css in the reference project was using both for page padding and section rhythm, and an undefined var() in a shorthand invalidates the WHOLE declaration silently -- the page simply had no padding and nothing reported it.
